world_update.actors: Country B’s capital instructs its delegation that it can support the memorandum in principle but wants clearer drafting on the definition of market‑stress indicators and confirmation that emergency suspensions and freezes will not be triggered lightly or used to create de facto permanent restrictions under the guise of safeguards.

rounds.reasoning_summary:
**Clarifying procedures for action**

I need to acknowledge that Country A has agreed on a process where emergency actions will only trigger after at least two indicators are confirmed, along with Secretariat validation. Provisional suspensions will take effect for a 72-hour initial review. Any suspension requires written reasons, periodic reviews every 72 hours, and must be publicly announced for transparency. I propose amending the language to include these points and recommend that Country B confirm this for prompt action.
rounds.response: Country A accepts tightening the chapeau: emergency indicators will be assessed cumulatively—no emergency action unless at least two pre‑defined indicators breach their thresholds and the Secretariat corroborates the data within 24 hours and the Sub‑Panel considers the recent historical context—isolated single‑metric deviations will not suffice. Provisional suspensions/freezes will take effect immediately for an initial 72‑hour period while the Emergency Sub‑Panel reviews and issues a reasoned recommendation; extensions are permitted only once for a further 72 hours and only by joint decision based on that recommendation, after which no further rollovers are allowed without an explicit positive endorsement. Any suspension must include a written rationale, public notice and scheduled 72‑hour reviews to guard against politicized or routine use. If Country B concurs with these amendments, Country A will instruct our capital to approve the revised text for signature and will constitute the working group within 48 hours so the memorandum can be validated in time to avoid the default regime.

rounds.consequence: Country A’s agreement to cumulative, time‑limited emergency triggers and to tighten safeguards against politicized or routine use reassures Country B that the provisional TRQs will not become a vehicle for open‑ended new restrictions. This clarification enables Country B’s delegation to seek a green light from its capital to proceed toward signature of the provisional implementing memorandum.

world_update.context: As the statutory deadline approaches, the secretariat circulates a short note outlining the remaining procedural steps—signature of the memorandum, validation of the annexes within seven days, and any necessary legislative notifications—that must be completed to activate the provisional TRQs before automatic reversion. Commentary from financial analysts increasingly assumes that a narrow interim deal on critical inputs will enter into force, though they stress that any last‑minute hesitation could still derail the process.
world_update.resource: The expectation that a tightly safeguarded TRQ arrangement for key semiconductor components and precision tooling will be signed and validated reduces perceived exposure of Country A’s manufacturers to abrupt supply disruptions. This prospect slightly eases the draw on Country A’s adjustment capacity, though buffers remain under strain given ongoing uncertainty about the broader default regime.
world_update.actors: Country B’s authorities instruct their delegation to confirm that, subject to the refined emergency‑adjustment language, they are prepared to recommend immediate signature of the memorandum. International observers prepare draft reports describing the emerging TRQ framework and its safeguards in detail, pending confirmation that both parties will sign and implement it fast enough to avoid the default.

rounds.antecedent: At what is expected to be the last formal meeting before the statutory deadline, the chair invites Country B to state its position on the revised memorandum and then calls on Country A’s head of delegation to confirm, for the record, its readiness to sign and to outline how its authorities intend to complete validation and activation within the compressed timetable.
